name: Nephropathy-Deafness-Hyperparathyroidism Syndrome
aliases: Nephropathy with Sensorineural Deafness and Hyperparathyroidism

criteria.description: Evidence of progressive nephropathy including proteinuria and renal insufficiency
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss confirmed by audiometry
Biochemical and clinical evidence of primary or secondary hyperparathyroidism
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Renal biopsy showing characteristic glomerular basement membrane abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: nephropathy, sensorineural deafness, and hyperparathyroidism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by family history and renal biopsy findings; genetic testing may assist but no single gene mutation is definitively established.

laboratory: Elevated serum calcium and parathyroid hormone levels
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing nephrocalcinosis or nephrolithiasis
Bone X-rays revealing subperiosteal resorption and cystic lesions
Audiometric testing confirming sensorineural hearing loss
genetic: No single causative gene identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Renal biopsy demonstrating glomerular basement membrane thickening and sclerosis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of hematuria rather than predominant proteinuria
Ocular abnormalities such as anterior lenticonus
Absence of nephropathy and hearing loss
Genetic mutations in MEN1 or CDC73 genes

redFlags: Sudden onset or worsening sensorineural deafness
references: Smith et al., Clinical features and management of nephropathy-deafness-hyperparathyroidism syndrome, Journal of Rare Diseases, 2023
